bibl.title: Distinct neural representations for prosocial and self-benefiting effort

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: The neural representation of effort cost when an act benefits another person rather than oneself, measured with grip force during fMRI.
span.quote: However, how the brain encodes effort costs when actions benefit others is unknown.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Strikingly, we identified a unique neural signature of effort in the anterior cingulate gyrus (ACCg) for prosocial acts, both when choosing to help others and when exerting force to benefit them.

span.label: effort-based prosocial decision-making
span.quote: However, how the brain encodes effort costs when actions benefit others is unknown.

span.label: fmri
span.quote: During fMRI, participants completed a decision-making task where they chose in each trial whether to “work” and exert force (30%–70% of maximum grip strength) or “rest” (no effort) for rewards (2–10 credits).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The ACCg represents the effort cost of helping in order to motivate the act and push the person past the barriers standing between another and a good outcome
span.quote: In particular, the ACCg may be crucial for motivating people to help others and overcome barriers to others receiving positive outcomes.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Resonating with another's emotional state strengthens how sharply the brain represents the cost of helping them, and that representation in turn sets how willing the person is to help
span.quote: Our findings demonstrate that representing how costly and effortful a prosocial behavior is may be linked to how strongly one represents the emotional states of others, which leads to variability in how willing people are to help others.

span.label: Effort discounting devalues reward as required force rises, and the paper's model gives the discount a separate rate for self and for other
span.quote: This phenomenon, referred to as effort discounting, relies on computations in which rewards are devalued by exerting effort.

span.label: The discount rate is steeper for others, so the same reward loses more of its value when the beneficiary is someone else
span.quote: Thus, as the required effort increased, the subjective value of decisions decreased at a higher rate when making prosocial versus self-benefiting choices.

span.label: The ACCg carries the prosocial effort code at both stages of the act - deciding whether to help, and energising the force once committed
span.quote: Multivariate patterns in the ACCg specifically encoded representations of prosocial effort when making a choice, and univariate signals scaled with how much effort was required, with no such signals for self-benefiting efforts.

span.label: Representing how costly a prosocial act is may be the missing link between feeling what others feel and actually helping them
span.quote: Our findings demonstrate that representing how costly and effortful a prosocial behavior is may be linked to how strongly one represents the emotional states of others, which leads to variability in how willing people are to help others.

span.label: Multivariate RSA can detect structure that univariate averaging destroys, which is why the social specificity shows up here and not in earlier work
span.quote: RSA can be more sensitive than univariate analysis since it captures effects that are washed away by averaging across voxels 59 but that are crucial for understanding social specialization.

span.label: If the VTA codes value only for self-benefiting effort, then a simple warm-glow account - helping is rewarding to the helper - cannot be the whole story
span.quote: Such findings concord with the idea that prosocial and self-benefiting actions are distinct, may be linked to partially distinct motivational processes, and suggest that perhaps “warm glow” is not always the driver of prosocial acts.

span.label: The design could not compare effort costs against other costs such as time because of protocol complexity
span.quote: Due to the complexity of our protocol and richness of experimental conditions, it was not possible to compare effort costs with these other costs.

span.label: The authors acknowledge a rival reading of the ACCg signal as reflecting stronger effort discounting for others rather than prosocial-specific effort coding
span.quote: However, an alternative explanation is that ACCg signals reflect stronger effort discounting for other.

span.label: Thirty-eight participants after exclusions, powered at 83% for the behavioural effect on the basis of a single prior study
span.quote: Based on the effect size from Lockwood et al., 9 a sample of 38 people gave 83% power to detect a significant behavioral effect.

span.label: The design rests on a deception, and participants who saw through it were excluded after scanning
span.quote: Two who did not believe the deception in the study set-up (see “ Role assignment ” details below), and one who never chose to exert effort for the other person.

span.label: The recipient is an anonymous stranger with no feedback or interaction, which the authors note is only one kind of prosocial situation
span.quote: In the real world outside of the lab, prosocial behaviors also often occur where people get direct feedback from others.

span.label: The VTA and self-benefiting value findings come from an exploratory whole-brain searchlight, not from the pre-specified regions of interest
span.quote: However, a whole-brain exploratory searchlight analysis revealed a significantly stronger correlation with the self-SV than other-SV model RDM in the midbrain, putatively in the VTA (x = 4, y = −22, z = 16, k = 291, Z = 4.45, p = 0.033, FWE-whole brain; Figure 5 A; Table S6 ) and the posterior cingulate (x = 20, y = −20, z = 50, Z = 4.78, k = 578, p = 0.002, FWE-whole brain corrected; Table S6 ).

span.label: The midbrain cluster is identified as VTA only approximately
span.quote: Notably, we also found a midbrain region, closely approximating the VTA, that contained a multivariate representation of SV exclusively when making choices to benefit oneself.

span.label: The design cannot separate valuing an option from choosing it, which the authors leave to methods with better timing
span.quote: In addition, there could be different neural signals that occur between valuing options when offered and when choosing to select them.

span.label: The brain-behaviour links are correlations across 38 people, and the authors note the known statistical problems with such correlations
span.quote: When linking these behaviors to neural responses, we focused on time points in the trial that were as independent as possible from the behavior, given the statistical issues with correlating individual behavior and neural signals.

span.label: Participants with previous psychology experience or prior participation in social studies were screened out, so the sample is selected against exactly the people most likely to detect the deception
span.quote: Our pre-scanning exclusion criteria were previous psychology experience, participation in social studies, left handedness, and neuro/psychiatric disorders.

span.label: the other player's identity was OBSCURED at the meeting at the start of the session
span.quote: with their identity obscured (to control for influences of identity or reciprocity

span.label: participants were told the bonus was up to five pounds but were NOT told the points-to-money exchange rate during the task
span.quote: were not made aware of the exchange rate while completing the task to ensure that they did not try to compute a running total.

span.label: affectively empathic → ACCg
span.note: BETWEEN-SUBJECTS ASSOCIATION FROM SELF-REPORT: individuals who reported being more affectively empathic represented the effort of behaviours more distinctly in the ACCg when deciding whether to act prosocially. A trait measure co-varying with a representational measure across people - no manipulation, no established direction, and no edge type for it.
span.quote: Therefore, individuals who reported being more affectively empathic represented the effort of behaviors more distinctly in the ACCg when deciding whether to act prosocially.

span.label: empathy - affective: resonating with the affect of others, and the only component that tracks the ACCg prosocial effort pattern
span.quote: An important distinction is often made in the literature between “affective empathy,” resonating with the affect of others, and “cognitive empathy,” understanding the thoughts and affective states of others.

span.label: empathy - cognitive: understanding others' thoughts and states, which shows no relation to the same pattern
span.quote: We found that affective empathy was positively correlated with the strength of prosocial effort patterns in ACCg (Pearson’s r (36) = 0.39, p = 0.02), whereas cognitive empathy was not (Pearson’s r (36) = 0.05, p = 0.78, correlations significantly different t = 2.04, p = 0.02).

span.label: effort - as decided: the cost weighed when choosing whether to work at all, measured at the offer stage
span.quote: Using this design, we could examine activity time locked to the points in the trial where people made a decision to work or rest and responses during the exertion of force ( Figure 1 ).

span.label: effort - as exerted: the force actually produced once committed, a separate measure at a separate time point
span.quote: A second critical aspect of helping others is that after we have decided to help, we have to energize our actions, and we have to exert the effort required.

span.label: prosocial coding - the WEAK sense: a region whose pattern correlates with the other-effort model, which four of four regions satisfy
span.quote: Multivariate patterns in our three other ROIs also showed significant correlations with the other-effort RDM when making prosocial choices (other-effort mean rank correlation τ A ± SE: TPJ = 0.033 ± 0.010, p = 0.001; AI = 0.021 ± 0.008, p = 0.006; dACC/dmPFC = 0.029 ± 0.008, p = 0.001).

span.label: prosocial coding - the STATED sense: correlates with other-effort, does NOT correlate with self-effort, and the two differ significantly - which only the ACCg satisfies
span.quote: For a region to be considered coding prosocial, and not self-benefiting, effort, its RDM should correlate with the other-effort model RDM, and not with the self-effort model RDM, and there should be a significant difference between the strength of those correlations.

span.label: specialisation - domain-general: the same code regardless of who benefits, which is what dACC/dmPFC and AI show for subjective value
span.quote: We show multivariate representations of SV are present in these same regions, regardless of whom the effort is being exerted for.

span.label: null result - as Bayesian support rather than absence of significance, used where the paper wants to assert no difference
span.quote: Importantly, there was no significant difference in success (exerting effort for at least 1 second of a 3-s period, fixed for each trial) between self (mean = 0.97) and other trials (mean = 0.97, Z = −0.88, r = 0.05 [0.00, 0.29], p = 0.38; Table 1 ) and Bayesian evidence for no difference (BF 01 = 4.19, substantial evidence in support of the null).

span.label: builds-on → Lockwood and colleagues (reference 9), the prior behavioural prosocial effort task
span.quote: Lockwood and colleagues 9 required participants to make decisions about whether they would rather take a rest for small reward (1 credit) or exert physical effort (30%–70% of their max grip strength) to obtain higher rewards (2–10 credits).

span.label: builds-on → Marr's three levels of analysis as applied to social specificity (reference 12)
span.quote: Recently, we highlighted how using the framework of Marr’s three levels can be fruitful for examining if a process is socially, or self, specific, either in how it is implemented in the brain, or in its algorithmic processes.

span.label: extends → Lockwood et al. (reference 9), the behavioural effort task this study puts in the scanner
span.quote: Here, to address the question of whether prosocial efforts are processed distinctly from self-benefiting ones, participants completed a physical effort task 9 where self-benefiting and prosocial decisions were dissociated.

span.label: supports → monkey neurophysiology showing ACCg neurons signalling exclusively when another receives reward
span.quote: Neurophysiological recordings in monkeys indicate that the ACCg contains a higher proportion of neurons that signal exclusively when another, not oneself, receives rewards compared with other frontal regions.

span.label: critiques → the inference from economic-game studies that AI and dACC/dmPFC activity is specifically prosocial
span.quote: This finding raises the possibility that these areas may be less directly linked to prosocial behavior and more linked to domain-general decision processes.

span.label: extends → Marr's three levels as a framework for testing whether a process is socially specific
span.quote: Recently, we highlighted how using the framework of Marr’s three levels can be fruitful for examining if a process is socially, or self, specific, either in how it is implemented in the brain, or in its algorithmic processes.

span.label: anterior cingulate gyrus —distinct-from→ dorsal anterior cingulate cortex
span.quote: These allowed us to probe distinct contributions of different portions of the cingulate cortex, distinguishing dorsal dACC/dmPFC (area 8 m) 18 , 24 , 28 from more ventral portions of the ACCg 12 , 36 , 37 , 61 ( Figure S4 ; STAR Methods ).

span.label: affective empathy —distinct-from→ cognitive empathy
span.quote: An important distinction is often made in the literature between “affective empathy,” resonating with the affect of others, and “cognitive empathy,” understanding the thoughts and affective states of others.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · effort —causes→ subjective value
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span defines the phenomenon - 'This phenomenon, referred to as effort discounting, relies on computations in which rewards are devalued by exerting effort' - names one endpoint, and carries NO EFFECT CUE, so a `causes` edge on it would fail the gate's causes test today. The replacement names both endpoints, states the effect, AND GIVES ITS DIRECTION: 'as the required effort INCREASED, the subjective value of decisions DECREASED at a higher rate when making prosocial versus self-benefiting choices.' Selected from the narrowed candidate pool (Q-372) after reading six offers and declining five - Cowan2008's offer contained the containment cue 'part of' but attached to 'THE FORMER' and 'THE LATTER', hiding both endpoints behind anaphors while its existing span says 'A SUBSET OF the activated information is the focus of attention' outright.
span.quote: This phenomenon, referred to as effort discounting, relies on computations in which rewards are devalued by exerting effort.

span.label: effort discounting —operationalised-as→ Bayesian information criterion
span.quote: The 2 Κ 1 β model also won in the majority of participants compared with other closely performing models in terms of Bayesian information criterion (BIC) scores ( Figures 2 C and S3 C).

span.label: effort —operationalised-as→ maximum voluntary contraction
span.quote: Before undergoing fMRI, participants were instructed to squeeze as hard as they could to measure their maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) on a handheld dynamometer to threshold each effort level to their own strength.

span.label: representational similarity analysis —operationalised-as→ representational dissimilarity matrices
span.quote: We calculated brain representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs) coding for dissimilarity (correlation distance 59 ) in multivariate patterns of voxels for all pairs of conditions.

span.label: multivariate —contrasted-with→ univariate
span.quote: These population codes cannot be captured in a univariate analysis that is based on the height of the BOLD signal, rather than the geometry (or similarity) between different experimental conditions.

span.label: representational similarity analysis —operationalised-as→ population code
span.quote: This is crucial as RSA is based on the knowledge that population codes of neurons or voxels represent information a “neural population code.”

span.label: prosocial —causes→ anterior cingulate gyrus
span.quote: In line with our hypothesis, the ACCg ROI carried a multivariate representation of effort on prosocial trials—other-effort mean rank correlation τ A ± SE: ACCg = 0.026 ± 0.009, p = 0.005, surviving FDR correction for 24 comparisons (6 models, 4 brain areas, 2 recipients)—and was the only ROI to display a significant difference between the other-effort and self-effort RDMs (Z = −2.73, effect size r = 0.44 [0.13, 0.69], p = 0.006; Figure 4 A).

span.label: RETRACTED (AN INDIVIDUAL-DIFFERENCES ASSOCIATION, TAGGED AS CAUSATION) · affective empathy —causes→ anterior cingulate gyrus
span.note: RETRACTED: AN INDIVIDUAL-DIFFERENCES ASSOCIATION, TAGGED AS CAUSATION. The edge is `affective empathy --causes--> anterior cingulate gyrus`. The span is a between-subjects correlation stated in full: 'INDIVIDUALS WHO REPORTED BEING MORE AFFECTIVELY EMPATHIC represented the effort of behaviors MORE DISTINCTLY in the ACCg when deciding whether to act prosocially.' Self-reported empathy co-varies with representational distinctness across people; nothing was manipulated and no direction is established - the trait does not cause the gyrus. The cue that passed it was `affect`, inside AFFECTIVELY. WHAT THE SPAN DOES SAY (Q-309): the association, housed below. Same family as the correlational rows counted in Q-344 - the schema has no type for a correlation.
span.quote: Therefore, individuals who reported being more affectively empathic represented the effort of behaviors more distinctly in the ACCg when deciding whether to act prosocially.

span.label: ventral tegmental area —operationalised-as→ subjective value
span.quote: Such findings suggest that the VTA is engaged exclusively in making choices about exerting effort to benefit oneself, and vAI tracks subjective value more closely during self-benefiting than other-benefiting decisions.

span.label: anterior insula —is-a→ domain general
span.quote: Such a finding supports the idea that neural processes in dACC/dmPFC and AI are an important component of motivated behavior across multiple domains.

span.label: temporo-parietal junction —part-of→ prosocial
span.quote: In addition, activity in a connected portion of the temporo-parietal junction (TPJ) has long been implicated in social cognition and prosocial behavior and encodes effort costs differently when behaviors switch from cooperation to competition.

span.label: warm glow —contrasted-with→ prosocial
span.quote: Such findings concord with the idea that prosocial and self-benefiting actions are distinct, may be linked to partially distinct motivational processes, and suggest that perhaps “warm glow” is not always the driver of prosocial acts.

span.label: anterior cingulate gyrus —contrasted-with→ temporo-parietal junction
span.quote: Critically, although TPJ, AI, and dACC/dmPFC also represented prosocial effort, they did not do so more strongly than for the self-effort RDMs (Wilcoxon two-sided signed-rank test, all p > 0.07).

span.label: effort —causes→ subjective value
span.quote: Thus, as the required effort increased, the subjective value of decisions decreased at a higher rate when making prosocial versus self-benefiting choices.

span.label: representational similarity analysis with rank correlation
span.term: representational similarity analysis with rank correlation
span.quote: Inferences were drawn by correlating each model RDM with each brain RDM using Kendall’s τ A .

span.label: generalized linear mixed-effects model
span.quote: For choices between the work and rest offers we coded choice as a binary outcome variable and ran a generalized linear mixed-effects model (GLMM).

span.label: linear mixed-effects model
span.quote: We used a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) to predict the force that participants exerted on each trial as a function of effort, reward, and their interactions ( STAR Methods ).

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test with effect size
span.term: Wilcoxon signed-rank test with effect size
span.quote: Due to the non-normal distribution of the Κ parameters, we compared discounting for self and other using a non-parametric Wilcoxon two-sided signed rank test and generated a standardized effect size ( r ) for this difference using the wilcox_effsize function from the rstatix package.

span.label: maximum likelihood estimation
span.quote: Models were fitted using maximum likelihood estimation using the MATLAB function fmincon.

span.label: Bayesian information criterion
span.quote: For formal model comparison, we report the Bayesian information criterion (BIC) based on the log-likelihood.

span.label: Pearson correlation
span.quote: We used Pearson correlations to test the link between QCAE scores and multivariate representations of prosocial effort in ACCg and compared correlations using the paired.r function from the psych package.

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: Both the GLMM of choices and LMM of force were fit by maximum likelihood and we tested the fixed effects for statistical significance using parametric bootstrapping (1000 simulations) with the mixed function.

span.label: permutation test with family-wise error correction
span.term: permutation test with family-wise error correction
span.quote: we performed non-parametric permutation tests to determine the cluster level for FWE correction

span.label: false discovery rate correction
span.quote: surviving FDR correction for 24 comparisons (6 models, 4 brain areas, 2 recipients)

span.label: Bayes factor
span.quote: Notably, the specificity for prosocial effort in the ACCg was not due to total differences for other and self-representations, as the ACCg represented other and self-offers as equally dissimilar ( STAR Methods ; Bayesian paired sample t test BF 01

span.label: statistical power analysis
span.quote: a sample of 38 people gave 83% power to detect a significant behavioral effect.

span.label: Kendall's tau
span.quote: Inferences were drawn by correlating each model RDM with each brain RDM using Kendall’s τ A .

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
span.quote: Data are represented as median ± SE, ∗∗∗ p < 0.001, Wilcoxon two-sided signed rank test.

span.label: Bayes factor
span.quote: and Bayesian evidence for no difference (BF 01 = 4.19, substantial evidence in support of the null)

span.label: false discovery rate
span.quote: surviving FDR correction for 24 comparisons (6 models, 4 brain areas, 2 recipients)

span.label: family-wise error correction
span.quote: and within this cluster, a partially overlapping sub-cluster also showed a significant effect coding force for other greater than self (x = −6, y = 24, z = 20, Z = 3.28, k = 41, p = 0.029, FWE-small volume corrected [SVC]; Figure 4 B).

span.label: Bayesian information criterion
span.quote: Bars show model BIC, proportions show the number of participants with the lowest BIC for model 7 compared with model 10.

span.label: odds ratio
span.quote: people were less willing to help others at higher effort levels (OR = 1.20, 95% CI = [1.03, 1.40], p = 0.01)

span.label: Pearson correlation
span.quote: The level of force exerted on other trials in turn was positively associated with the strength of prosocial effort patterns in ACCg (Pearson’s r (36) = 0.38, p = 0.02).

span.label: linear mixed-effects model
span.quote: We used a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) to predict the force that participants exerted on each trial as a function of effort, reward, and their interactions ( STAR Methods ).

span.label: maximum likelihood estimation
span.quote: Next, we fit and compared a range of different models of effort discounting to participants’ choice behavior using maximum likelihood estimation ( STAR Methods ).

span.label: The anterior cingulate gyrus carried an effort signature specific to prosocial acts, present both when choosing to help and when exerting force for another person.
span.quote: Strikingly, we identified a unique neural signature of effort in the anterior cingulate gyrus (ACCg) for prosocial acts, both when choosing to help others and when exerting force to benefit them.

span.label: ACCg multivoxel patterns tracked the effort level of prosocial trials.
span.quote: In line with our hypothesis, the ACCg ROI carried a multivariate representation of effort on prosocial trials

span.label: Although TPJ, anterior insula and dACC/dmPFC also represented prosocial effort, only the ACCg represented it more strongly for others than for the self.
span.quote: Thus, although all ROIs showed significant correlations between the brain and model RDMs for the other-effort condition, it was only in the ACCg that showed a stronger pattern, relative to the self-benefiting condition.

span.label: The ventral tegmental area and ventral insula represented subjective value preferentially for self-benefiting rather than prosocial choices.
span.quote: In contrast, the ventral tegmental area and ventral insula represented value preferentially when choosing for oneself and not for prosocial acts.

span.label: The dACC/dmPFC and anterior insula carried subjective-value representations irrespective of who benefited, i.e. domain-generally.
span.quote: We show multivariate representations of SV are present in these same regions, regardless of whom the effort is being exerted for.

span.label: Participants accepted the effortful work option less often when the reward went to another person than when it went to themselves.
span.quote: Therefore, participants were less willing to exert effort to reward other people than themselves.

span.label: The fitted discount parameter was steeper for other than for self, so reward lost subjective value faster with effort on prosocial trials.
span.quote: Thus, as the required effort increased, the subjective value of decisions decreased at a higher rate when making prosocial versus self-benefiting choices.

span.label: The winning model gave higher K (steeper discounting) values for other than for self.
span.quote: Comparing discount parameters for self and other from the winning model showed significantly higher K values for other

span.label: Once they had chosen to help, participants squeezed with less force for others than for themselves, especially at high effort levels, yet succeeded equally often.
span.quote: Therefore, participants applied less force for other-benefiting than self-benefiting decisions, particularly at high effort levels, but were not less successful.

span.label: The strength of the ACCg prosocial-effort pattern tracked self-reported affective empathy.
span.quote: We found that affective empathy was positively correlated with the strength of prosocial effort patterns in ACCg

span.label: People with stronger ACCg representations of others' effort were both more empathic and exerted more force on prosocial trials.
span.quote: Together, these results suggest that individuals with stronger patterns of others effort in ACCg were higher in empathy and exerted more subsequent force into prosocial acts.

span.label: people were less willing to work for others, especially at higher effort and lower reward
span.quote: We observed significant recipient ∗ effort and recipient ∗ reward interactions showing that people were less willing to help others at higher effort levels (OR = 1.20, 95% CI = [1.03, 1.40], p = 0.01) and lower reward levels (OR = 1.31 [1.11, 1.55], p = 0.003).

span.label: the effort discount parameter was more than twice as steep for others as for self
span.quote: Comparing discount parameters for self and other from the winning model showed significantly higher K values for other (median = 0.15) than for self (median = 0.07, Z = −5.34, r = 0.50 [0.30, 0.65], p < 0.001; Figure 2 F).

span.label: people also exerted less actual force for others, yet were no less successful at hitting the target
span.quote: Therefore, participants applied less force for other-benefiting than self-benefiting decisions, particularly at high effort levels, but were not less successful.

span.label: only the ACCg met the paper's stated criterion for coding prosocial effort, though four regions met the weaker one
span.quote: Thus, although all ROIs showed significant correlations between the brain and model RDMs for the other-effort condition, it was only in the ACCg that showed a stronger pattern, relative to the self-benefiting condition.

span.label: the same ACCg region also tracked required force during exertion, but only on prosocial trials
span.quote: A univariate analysis time locked to the onset of the force period showed a cluster within the ACCg ROI that tracked amount of effort required specifically when making prosocial decisions (x = −6, y = 24, z = 20, Z = 3.28, k = 41, p = 0.029, FWE-SVC).

span.label: no brain region responded more to self force than to other force anywhere in the brain
span.quote: No brain areas significantly responded more to the contrast self force greater than other force at the whole-brain level or in any of our ROIs.

span.label: the strength of the ACCg prosocial effort pattern tracked affective but not cognitive empathy
span.quote: We found that affective empathy was positively correlated with the strength of prosocial effort patterns in ACCg (Pearson’s r (36) = 0.39, p = 0.02), whereas cognitive empathy was not (Pearson’s r (36) = 0.05, p = 0.78, correlations significantly different t = 2.04, p = 0.02).

span.label: the VTA carried subjective value only for self-benefiting choices, in an exploratory searchlight
span.quote: A cluster putatively in the ventral tegmental area (VTA) encoded representational patterns of subjective value exclusively on self-benefiting trials (x = 4, y = −22, z = 16, k = 291, Z = 4.45, p = 0.03, FWE-whole brain corrected after thresholding at p < 0.001).

span.label: dACC/dmPFC and AI carried subjective value for both self and other, in both multivariate and univariate analyses
span.quote: We found significant correlations between the self-SV and other-SV RDMs in dACC/dmPFC and AI (self-SV mean rank correlation τ A ± SE: dACC/dmPFC = 0.063 ± 0.012, p < 0.001; AI = 0.047 ± 0.012, p < 0.001; other-SV mean rank correlation τ A ± SE: dACC/dmPFC = 0.073 ± 0.012, p < 0.001; AI = 0.051 ± 0.013, p < 0.001; all survive FDR correction; Figure 6 A).

span.label: participants took longer to decide when the reward was for someone else
span.quote: Participants also took longer to choose between work and rest when rewards were for another person (other mean = 1.16 s versus self mean = 1.07 s , Z = −4.62, r = 0.19 [0.02, 0.41], p < 0.001; Table 1 ).

span.label: the ACCg specificity was not an artefact of it representing other-trials more distinctly overall
span.quote: Notably, the specificity for prosocial effort in the ACCg was not due to total differences for other and self-representations, as the ACCg represented other and self-offers as equally dissimilar ( STAR Methods ; Bayesian paired sample t test BF 01 = 4.61, substantial evidence in support of the null).

span.label: prosocial behaviors
span.quote: Prosocial behaviors—actions that benefit others—are central to individual and societal well-being.

span.label: effort discounting
span.quote: This phenomenon, referred to as effort discounting, relies on computations in which rewards are devalued by exerting effort.

span.label: affective empathy vs cognitive empathy
span.quote: An important distinction is often made in the literature between “affective empathy,” resonating with the affect of others, and “cognitive empathy,” understanding the thoughts and affective states of others.

span.label: empathy
span.quote: Empathy is the ability to vicariously experience and understand the affect of other people.

span.quote: For a region to be considered coding prosocial, and not self-benefiting, effort, its RDM should correlate with the other-effort model RDM, and not with the self-effort model RDM, and there should be a significant difference between the strength of those correlations.

span.label: physical effort (operational definition)
span.quote: Physical effort was operationalized as the amount of force participants exerted on a handheld dynamometer.

span.quote: “affective empathy,” resonating with the affect of others

span.quote: “cognitive empathy,” understanding the thoughts and affective states of others

span.quote: For a region to be considered coding prosocial, and not self-benefiting, effort, its RDM should correlate with the other-effort model RDM, and not with the self-effort model RDM, and there should be a significant difference between the strength of those correlations.

span.label: representational dissimilarity matrix
span.quote: We calculated brain representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs) coding for dissimilarity (correlation distance 59 ) in multivariate patterns of voxels for all pairs of conditions.

span.term: effort level required by the work offer
span.quote: Effort ranged from 30-70% (in 10% increments) of the participants’ MVC.

span.label: reward magnitude on offer
span.quote: Higher-reward, higher-effort offers varied from 2-10 points (in 2-point increments).
